data.long_meaning: In Irish mythology, Eithne was the goddess of the earth and fertility. Her name is possibly derived from the Greek 'Aineia' or 'Eirene', meaning 'peace'. In Christian tradition, Eithne is mentioned in the 'Life of St. Patrick' as the mother of the Irish chieftain Dagda. The name Eithne carries the meaning “Goddess of the earth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Eithne usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Eithne, the mother of St. Patrick's Irish convert, became a symbol of the spiritual transformation that took place during the early Christianization of Ireland. Her name stands as a reminder of the peace and calm that can be found through faith and a connection to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Saint Eithne or Ita (d. 640) was an Irish abbess and one of the most venerated saints of the Early Middle Ages.
historical_references.context: Eithne, also known as Ita, was born into a wealthy family in County Kildare, Ireland. She is best known for founding the monastic site at Killeedy and caring for St. Brigid, who was a foster-child in her family. Eithne was renowned for her piety and miraculous abilities, and became a respected spiritual leader in her own right.

historical_references.reference: Saint Eithne (d. 750) was an Irish princess and abbess, who is venerated as a patron saint of Kinsale, County Cork.
historical_references.context: Eithne, also known as Ita or Ethne, was the daughter of King Eoghan of Desmond. She was raised in the court of her uncle, King Finaegh, and was said to have been a great beauty. Eithne renounced the world and became a nun, and later founded a monastery in Kinsale. She is remembered for her generosity and her many miracles.

Her story is commonly told in Celtic folklore, where she is portrayed as the wife of the god Dagda. In Wiccan practices, Eithne is sometimes invoked as a goddess of fertility, passion, and transformation. Her name is gaining popularity on various platforms such as Reddit, where her story and symbolism are often discussed in pagan and mythology communities.
